Decimal (base 10) Time

      In the case of based time, using base 10, the day is divided into 10 “hours”, each “hour” into 100 “minutes”, and each “minute” into 100 “seconds”. In base 10 itself, the day is divided into 10:100:100;

      For both the Standard Full Day and the base 10 analogue displays, 0 is midnight, and the bottom hafl of the display roughly represents night, and the top half, day; the top center number in each case is noon; this also means that the “hour” hand roughly indicates the Sun’s position in the sky.

      The smaller display represents how it could be seen from a distance, or a minimalist watch face.

      One base 10 “hour” is 12⁄5 = 2.4 = 02:24 standard hours exactly; 1 “minute” is 36⁄25 = 1.44 = 01:26.4 min; and 1 “second” is 108⁄125 = 0.865 s

      The 10 “hours” marks are relatively close to the standard 12 hours marks on the analogue display, but there are now 5⁄3 = 1..6 times more “minutes”, so, the “hours” occupy 36° of the circle, and each “minute and “second”, 3.6°; compare this with standard hours with 30° for the 12h display, and 15° for the 24h display; standard minutes and seconds take 6° each.

       Adaptations to the analogue display have then to be made: since the “minutes” are so narrow, the display works best if an extra hand is added; the adaptations have to be physically distinguishable enough so as not to confuse the eyes; colour, of course, will not always be an available option, and, for the extra hand, thickness alone, or length, from a distance or in tiny detail, might not work.
